frontend.state_management: React Context + useReducer (no Redux unless needed at scale)
frontend.rationale: React mandated by product. TypeScript for maintainability at scale. Tailwind + shadcn for rapid UI development. Context for simple state (no cross-module complexity yet). React Hook Form for form-heavy module (farmer profiles, listings, messaging). Axios familiar and reliable. React Router v6 standard. Vite for fast dev experience.

backend.rationale: Spring Boot and Java mandated. JWT for stateless REST API. Spring Security for OAuth2-ready auth layer. Spring Data JPA + Hibernate standard for SQL mapping. Bean Validation for request validation. Springdoc for API documentation (required for integration partners).

database.cache_rationale: Not needed for MVP (1,000 users, no real-time streaming). Can add Redis later if search/browse queries become bottleneck.
database.rationale: MySQL mandated by product. Flyway for simple, versionable migrations. No caching layer required for initial scale—MySQL with proper indexing on search fields (farmer name, produce type, location) is sufficient.

frontend.rationale: Static React build hosted in S3, distributed via CloudFront CDN. Simple, cost-effective, mandated AWS.

backend.platform: AWS ECS Fargate or EC2 + ALB
backend.rationale: Docker-based deployment (product mandated). Fargate for serverless simplicity, or EC2 with load balancer for predictable cost. Auto-scaling for traffic spikes during launch.

database.rationale: Managed MySQL on AWS. Multi-AZ for availability. Automated backups. Mandated AWS.

email_notifications.use_cases: Order confirmations, payment receipts, farmer inquiries, review notifications
email_notifications.rationale: Integrated with AWS. Simple setup. Sufficient for transactional emails.

payment_processing.abstraction: PaymentProcessor interface (backend). Route requests to processor via abstraction. Webhook handlers for payment status updates.
payment_processing.rationale: Payment processor not yet chosen (open question in requirements). Define adapter interface to support any processor. Implementations can be swapped without changing core order flow.

third_party_logistics.abstraction: LogisticsProvider interface (backend). Methods: createShipment(), trackShipment(), getDeliveryEstimate(). Provider-specific implementations.
third_party_logistics.integration_points: Order confirmation → create shipment; Order tracking page → fetch status from provider
third_party_logistics.rationale: Third-party provider not yet chosen (open question). Define adapter to support any logistics partner. Platform coordinates timing but does not handle delivery itself.

file_storage.use_cases: Farmer profile photos, produce listing photos
file_storage.rationale: Integrated with AWS. Pre-signed URLs for secure uploads/downloads. Simple integration with backend.

analytics.metrics: Order volume, user acquisition rate, farmer engagement, AOV tracking
analytics.rationale: Not mandated by requirements but useful for tracking success metrics. Can be added post-launch.

core_entities: Produce (type, quantity, harvest_date, lead_time, price, photos, availability)
Order (customer, produce items, total, address, payment_status, delivery_status)
data_model_overview.data_characteristics: Moderate volume (1,000 users → ~5,000-10,000 orders in first 90 days). Relational (orders → customers, farmers, produce). File references (S3 URLs). Simple temporal (order dates, delivery windows). No real-time streaming or complex aggregations needed for MVP.

key_controls: JWT tokens + Spring Security (A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures)
Input validation via Bean Validation (A03:2021 - Injection)
SQL parameterized queries via Hibernate (A03:2021 - Injection)
HTTPS/TLS for all communication (A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures)
CORS configured per origin (A01:2021 - Broken Access Control)
Secrets stored in AWS Secrets Manager (A06:2021 - Vulnerable and Outdated Components)
Rate limiting on payment/login endpoints (A05:2021 - Broken Access Control)

deployment_pipeline.frontend: Git → GitHub Actions → npm build → S3 upload → CloudFront invalidation
deployment_pipeline.backend: Git → GitHub Actions → Maven build → Docker build → ECR push → ECS/EC2 deploy → smoke tests
deployment_pipeline.database: Git → Flyway migrations → RDS schema update (on deployment)
deployment_pipeline.rationale: Simple CI/CD. GitHub Actions integrated with AWS. Docker for consistent environments.

monitoring_and_logging.backend_logs: CloudWatch Logs (Spring Boot logs → CloudWatch via Docker)
monitoring_and_logging.frontend_errors: Optional: Sentry or CloudWatch for JS errors
monitoring_and_logging.database: RDS CloudWatch metrics (connections, CPU, disk I/O)
monitoring_and_logging.success_metric_tracking: Custom CloudWatch dashboards for: user acquisition, weekly active rate, AOV

open_decisions: Payment processor: Razorpay (India-first) or Stripe (global). Architect to abstract via adapter.
Logistics partner(s): Confirm integration API and SLA before implementation.
KYC/customer verification: Policy decision needed. Implement via validation layer.
Food safety compliance: Legal review needed. May require disclaimers or regulatory integrations.
notes.simplicity_priority: This stack is intentionally minimal—no message queue (Kafka), no microservices, no complex caching. Scale vertically first (RDS, ECS compute), add horizontal complexity only if metrics demand it.
notes.mvp_focus: All choices target rapid launch and clear paths to the three success metrics: 1,000 users, 50% weekly active, ₹500+ AOV.
